title: ～ようになる — come to be able to ～, begin to ～
summary: Shows a change from not being able to do something, or not doing it, to being able to or doing it: “come to ～.” It attaches to the dictionary form or potential form of a verb. It is common for skills, habits and gradual changes.

patterns.form: 動詞可能形 ＋ ようになる
patterns.gloss: potential form + ようになる: 泳げるようになる (become able to swim)

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形 ＋ ようになる
patterns.gloss: dictionary form + ようになる: 食べるようになる (begin to eat)

body.p: With the potential form, it says an ability was acquired, usually through practice: 泳げるようになりました (I became able to swim). The negative-to-positive change is the point; it does not describe a one-time event.
With other verbs, it says a new habit or situation began: 朝ごはんを食べるようになった. The changes are gradual, and the past ようになった is often used to describe how things are now. For the opposite, use ～なくなる.

examples.ja: 毎日（まいにち）練習（れんしゅう）して、泳（およ）げるようになりました。
examples.romaji: Mainichi renshū shite, oyogeru yō ni narimashita.
examples.tr: I practiced every day and became able to swim.

examples.ja: 練習（れんしゅう）して、自転車（じてんしゃ）に乗（の）れるようになった。
examples.romaji: Renshū shite, jitensha ni noreru yō ni natta.
examples.tr: After practicing, I became able to ride a bicycle.

examples.ja: 最近（さいきん）、朝（あさ）早（はや）く起（お）きられるようになりました。
examples.romaji: Saikin, asa hayaku okirareru yō ni narimashita.
examples.tr: Lately I've become able to wake up early in the morning.

pitfalls: For nouns and adjectives, use ～になる / ～くなる instead: 上手になる, 大きくなる.
Not for a deliberate decision; that is ～ことにする. ようになる describes a natural change.
